title: Impact of FDA Drug Approval on Biotech Company Returns

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
The appropriate method for analyzing the impact of FDA drug approval on the cumulative abnormal returns (CAR) of biotech companies is the Event Study methodology. This approach leverages the time dimension around the event (FDA approval). We compare the actual returns of the stocks to their expected returns (usually calculated using the market model) to determine abnormal returns, and subsequently aggregate these abnormal returns over a chosen window to compute the CAR.

Key assumption: The abnormal returns are accurately estimated, and any changes in stock returns around the event window are attributed to the event itself, provided there are no other confounding events affecting the stock during the period.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load necessary library
library(dplyr)

# Read the dataset
data <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s63_data.csv")

# Calculate abnormal returns
data <- data %>%
  mutate(ar = ret - (beta * mkt_ret))

# Define event window and estimation window
event_window <- -5:5  # 5 days before and after the event
estimation_window <- -20:-6  # Pre-event window for estimation of normal performance

# Function to calculate CAR over the event window for each stock
calculate_car <- function(data, stock_id, event_window) {
  stock_data <- data %>% filter(stock_id == stock_id)
  
  # Calculate abnormal return for each day in the event window
  ar_window <- stock_data %>% filter(event_day %in% event_window) %>% pull(ar)
  
  # Calculate CAR
  CAR <- sum(ar_window, na.rm = TRUE)
  return(CAR)
}

# Calculate CAR for each stock
cars <- data %>%
  group_by(stock_id) %>%
  summarize(CAR = calculate_car(data, unique(stock_id), event_window))

# Summary statistics of CAR
car_summary <- cars %>% summarize(mean_CAR = mean(CAR), sd_CAR = sd(CAR), n = n())

# Print results
print(car_summary)

# Basic robustness check: Check for pre-event abnormal returns (should be near zero)
pre_event_check <- data %>%
  filter(event_day %in% estimation_window) %>%
  summarize(pre_event_AR_mean = mean(ar, na.rm = TRUE))

print(pre_event_check)
```

## 3. Expected Findings
I expect a positive CAR because FDA drug approvals are generally viewed positively by the market, as they signal potentially increased future earnings for the company. The magnitude of the CAR will depend on the specific characteristics of the companies and the drugs approved, but it might typically be in the range of several percentage points, say around 2-5%, on average, over the defined event window.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Exploit the timing of FDA drug approval announcements as a natural experiment.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: FDA drug approvals lead to a positive change in biotech companies' CAR.
